newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up in line with CBOT soy complex.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up in line with CBOT soy complex.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended higher, in line with a dramatic turnaround in CBOT soybean prices that ended on the upside, traders said.
Canola, flax and feed grains started off in the minus column but midday buying mostly by commercials, erased those losses.
"This (canola) market just followed Chicago," one trader said. "We had some good buying at the lows of the day and when Chicago started climbing, we went with it."
But he noted the fundamentals remained bearish.
"The Canadian dollar is strong and that makes our exports more expensive," the trader said. January canola was up $2.20 at $395.00 and January flax climbed $4.00 at $364.50.
"Commercials played both sides of the market and ended up net buyers," the trader said. Flax had the same scenario."
Western barley finished with pared losses aided by light commission house buy stops, local short covering and support from CBOT corn and soybeans, another trader said.
A rally in Chicago wheat futures also supported feed grains, traders said. Selling dried up around midday when commission house buying with no available offers pushed prices higher, he said.
February western barley was off $0.50 at $138.30 and December feed wheat firmed $0.80 at $164.50.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
